Definition: from G5196; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:--use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hybrízō where we would say to insult, to abuse, to treat shamefully. In Matthew 22:6, the text says "and entreated [them] spitefully." In Luke 11:45, the text says "thus saying thou reproachest us also."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hybrízō to mean that pride is the oldest sin, and it always ends the same way — brought low. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Wedding Feast; Paul and Barnabas at Iconium
